$comment: Types every view-props file may name, and the plan every view receives beside its data. Drafted 09/10/2026 from Salt for Next.js 0.11.0's SectionPlan and block data types, renamed where the contract's field names differ.

plan.description: The page plan's view of one section: what the section cannot know about itself because it depends on the page (section#heading-level, section#anchors, section#priority-media).

props.name: index
props.description: The section's position among the page's rendered sections, from 0. Names per-section groups, such as an accordion's name.

props.name: anchor
props.description: The section's settled id, <anchor> (SC-012 to SC-014). Every section has one, so it is never null.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: 1 when the section claims the page's h1 (section#single-h1), otherwise 2.

props.name: headingId
props.description: <anchor>__heading when the section provides a heading, which the heading carries and the wrapper's aria-labelledby names; otherwise null.

props.name: bodyBaseLevel
props.description: The level a body's own headings count from (section#body-heading-base): the section heading's level, or the level it would have had.

props.name: priorityMedia
props.description: True for the one section on the page whose first image is the priority image: eager, fetchpriority high, never lazy (SC-007).

props.name: collapseTop
props.description: True when the section's top space is dropped to butt against the one above (section#adjacent-collapse).

props.name: settings
props.description: The wrapper settings, normalised: every value inside its vocabulary.

settings.description: The shared wrapper settings (contract/fields/_section-settings.json) as the wrapper draws them. The wrapper is the logic's, not the view's; a view reads these only to adapt to its band.

props.name: toneDark
props.description: The dark tone resolved: auto becomes the tone it stands for, so a view never sees auto.

props.name: backgroundImage
props.description: Null unless an image is set and resolves.

background.description: A section's background image, as the wrapper draws it.

image.description: A resolved image, ready for one img element (SC-007): the platform's image pipeline has chosen its formats and widths. contract/markup/media.json says how it is drawn.

props.name: alt
props.description: The image's own alt text; empty when it has none, which draws it as decorative.

point.description: A focal point, as percentages of the image's width and height.

link.description: A resolved link: an internal link already turned into its address. A link that does not resolve is dropped by the logic, so a view never draws a dead one.

button.description: A link drawn as a button, with its style.

card.description: One item of a collection, as a card draws it (contract/markup/card.json). What a card carries depends on its source; a value the source lacks, or the section switched off, is null.

props.name: href
props.description: The item's own page, for a source whose items have one.

props.name: meta
props.description: A role, a client or a byline, by source.

props.name: date
props.description: An ISO 8601 date, for a source whose items are dated.

tag.description: A category term on a card.

nextjs.owes: anchor in place of the nullable anchorId; bodyBaseLevel on the plan in place of the bodyBaseLevel() helper; the resolved image shape in place of StoredMedia's media reference; the resolved toneDark and backgroundImage in settings

wordpress.owes: the logic and view split itself (the ruling of 06/10/2026 on the Salt page): each section's template takes these props in $args and does no querying, sanitising or schema of its own
